text: Lark-5 listens on port 7864; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Lark-5, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Osprey-2 is Go. Nobody should assume the language of Osprey-2 applies to Lark-5, the language differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Questions about Kestrel-4 start with its owner, the Ember team; they triage anything filed against it. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Osprey-2, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Avocet-3 is Wendell Fairbanks. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Avocet-3 applies to Osprey-2, the pager rotation differs.
Unlike Osprey-2, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Lark-5 is the Tessera team. Nobody should assume the owner of Lark-5 applies to Osprey-2, the owner differs.
The yearly budget for Osprey-2 is $2730k, covering licences and hosting.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Kestrel-4, which is 1000 requests per minute.
Finance fixed the budget of Avocet-3 at $1335k, reviewed every quarter.

Unlike Egret-9, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Kestrel-4 is the Osaka datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Kestrel-4 applies to Egret-9, the datacenter differs.

Unlike Heron-6, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Osprey-2 is March 11, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Osprey-2 applies to Heron-6, the retirement date differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
The language of Egret-9 is Erlang, which new contributors must know. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Avocet-3 has one owner, the Keystone team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Celia Ivanova is on the pager rotation of Lark-5 this month, with a deputy as backup. An older draft of this note was archived.
